Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Blue mussels and ribbed mussels

Elders distinguished food gathering from caring for the shore. Blue mussels were preferred for eating, while ribbed or “bank” mussels were often left because they held the shore together. Shells from both were used as jewelry.1

The table lists Shinnecock Bay and the Atlantic beside blue mussels, and Heady Crick and Mecox Bay beside ribbed mussels.1

Places named in the catalogue

Shinnecock Bay; Atlantic Ocean; Heady Crick; Mecox Bay.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.
